title: Guacamole
subtitle: Fresh avocado dip with lime and coriander
excerpt: Ripe avocados mashed with lime, fresh coriander, green chilli and finely diced tomato. The texture should be chunky rather than smooth, with pieces of avocado still visible throughout. This takes 10 minutes and needs to be made as close to serving as possible since avocado oxidises quickly once cut.
sourceNotes: Guacamole has been made in Mexico since at least the 16th century when Spanish explorers encountered the Aztec sauce 'ahuacamolli'; the name comes from the Nahuatl words for avocado and sauce.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Press cling film directly onto the surface and refrigerate for up to 1 hour. The lime juice slows oxidation but won't stop it entirely.

content.text: Ripe avocados are non-negotiable. Press the pointed end gently: it should give slightly but not feel mushy. Under-ripe avocados are chalky and tasteless; overripe ones are brown and stringy. If you have a pestle and mortar, use it to crush the onion and chilli first with a pinch of salt before adding the avocado. This bruises rather than blends, giving a better texture. A fork on a plate works just as well if you don't have one.

items.prepNote: ripe, halved, stoned and flesh scooped out
finely chopped, seeds removed for less heat

content.text: If using a pestle and mortar, add the diced onion, green chilli and a large pinch of salt. Pound to a rough paste. This mellows the raw onion and distributes the heat from the chilli evenly through the dip.
Add the avocado flesh and mash with the pestle or a fork. Leave it chunky; this is not a smooth puree. Add the lime juice and mash briefly to combine.
Fold in the diced tomato and fresh coriander. Taste and adjust salt, lime and chilli. The dip should taste bright and fresh, with the lime clearly present.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips, or press cling film directly onto the surface and refrigerate for up to 1 hour. The lime juice will slow browning but won't stop it entirely.

items.cause: Avocado flesh was exposed to air too long before or after mashing
items.fix: Scrape off the brown surface layer; the flesh underneath will still be green and fine. Next time add lime juice immediately as you mash and press cling film directly on the surface.

items.cause: Not enough salt or lime, or the avocados were slightly under-ripe
items.fix: Add more salt and lime juice in small amounts, stirring and tasting after each addition. A pinch of cumin can also help lift the flavour.
